title: Fix trace hover tooltip labels and positioning
description: Fixes trace hover tooltip labels to prefer associated trace names over pad-selector display names, adjusts tooltip size and positioning, and adds regression tests for label preference and formatting.
body:
## Summary

- prefer an associated trace or net name over the pad-selector display name
- show `mm` only when a numeric trace length is available, while preserving selector text as a fallback label
- make the trace tooltip smaller and offset it from the cursor
- add regression coverage for label preference, missing lengths, max-length formatting, and over-length state

## Root cause

Trace hover formatting appended the unit and selector-based `display_name` whenever connection information existed, even when `trace_length` was absent. The tooltip was also centered horizontally on the pointer with a 14px font and minimum width, which made it feel oversized and overlap the cursor.

## Impact

Trace hover labels are more readable, named traces are easier to identify, and missing length data no longer produces labels such as `mm (...)`.

## Validation

- `bun test` (38 tests pass)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json`
- `bun run build`
- `bunx biome check src/lib/get-trace-overlay-text.ts src/components/ElementOverlayBox.tsx tests/lib/get-trace-overlay-text.test.ts`

title: Add C284163 crystal import repro
description: Add the real EasyEDA fixture for JLCPCB part C284163, which includes focused characterization coverage showing the current importer emits the four-pad 24 MHz crystal as a generic chip
body:
## Summary

- add the real EasyEDA fixture for JLCPCB part C284163 (`TXM24M0004252BBCEO00T`)
- add focused characterization coverage showing the current importer emits the four-pad 24 MHz crystal as a generic `<chip>`

## Why

The EasyEDA source identifies the part with the `X?` reference prefix, a `CRYSTAL-SMD_4P` package, a `24MHz` value, and four numbered pads. The current component classifier has no crystal output type, so generated TSX uses `ChipProps` and `<chip>`. This loses crystal-specific semantics even though current tscircuit core supports four-pin crystals.

The fixture does not contain a load-capacitance value. The follow-up fix must not invent one.

This is the reproduction base of a two-PR stack. It intentionally changes no production code.

title: Preserve circular EasyEDA SMT pads
description: Summary Fixes EasyEDA ELLIPSE SMT pads being converted to rectangular tscircuit pads. Closes the regression reproduced in 429.  Root cause The SMT-pad conversion explicitly mapped EasyEDA ELLIPSE to rect, changing circular copper lands into square pads.  Fix Map EasyEDA ELLIPSE SMT pads to tscircuit circle pads. Convert the C2055640 expected-failure repro into a passing regression test. Update affected TSX and PCB snapshots to render circular pads. The stored fixture corpus contains 665 non-drilled ELLIPSE pads. All have equal width and height, so the circle representation preserves their source geometry. This includes: C2055640: 100 UFBGA pads. C2943786: 565 BGA pads.  Impact The converter now preserves the physical copper geometry of EasyEDA circular SMTBGA lands instead of adding square corners. Generated TSX uses shapecircle and a radius derived from the source pad diameter.  Validation bunx tsc --noEmit bun run format:check C2055640 conversion tests: 2 passing C2943786 conversion test: passing with 565 circular pads C2055640 courtyard and C1555 footprint snapshot tests: passing Full suite: 128 passing; remaining failures were unrelated pre-existing 5-second render timeouts during the serial local run
body:
## Summary

Fixes EasyEDA `ELLIPSE` SMT pads being converted to rectangular tscircuit pads.

Closes the regression reproduced in #429.

## Root cause

The SMT-pad conversion explicitly mapped EasyEDA `ELLIPSE` to `rect`, changing circular copper lands into square pads.

## Fix

- Map EasyEDA `ELLIPSE` SMT pads to tscircuit `circle` pads.
- Convert the C2055640 expected-failure repro into a passing regression test.
- Update affected TSX and PCB snapshots to render circular pads.

The stored fixture corpus contains 665 non-drilled `ELLIPSE` pads. All have equal width and height, so the circle representation preserves their source geometry. This includes:

- C2055640: 100 UFBGA pads.
- C2943786: 565 BGA pads.

## Impact

The converter now preserves the physical copper geometry of EasyEDA circular SMT/BGA lands instead of adding square corners. Generated TSX uses `shape="circle"` and a radius derived from the source pad diameter.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- C2055640 conversion tests: 2 passing
- C2943786 conversion test: passing with 565 circular pads
- C2055640 courtyard and C1555 footprint snapshot tests: passing
- Full suite: 128 passing; remaining failures were unrelated pre-existing 5-second render timeouts during the serial local run

title: Fix duplicate EasyEDA symbol pin mapping
description: Fixes the issue of duplicate EasyEDA symbol pin numbers by mapping them to unused footprint ports, ensuring each schematic port corresponds to a unique footprint pin.
body:
## Summary
- prevent duplicate EasyEDA symbol pin numbers from reusing an already-mapped footprint port
- map malformed duplicate pins to the remaining unused footprint port
- turn the C113367 repro from #428 into a passing regression test and update its snapshots

## Root cause
C113367 assigns both VO_NEG and NC to EasyEDA pin 8. The converter accepted pin 8 twice, producing schematic pins `[1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8]` and omitting footprint pin 4.

## Result
NC now falls back to unused footprint pin 4, producing one schematic port for every footprint pin: `[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]`.

## Validation
- `bun test --timeout 60000` — 139 pass, 0 fail
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- focused regression tests — 8 pass, 0 fail

Follow-up fix for #428.

title: Preserve exact manufacturer part numbers
description: Preserves the exact EasyEDA manufacturer part number in generated component metadata and reports a clear conversion error when EasyEDA does not provide a manufacturer part number instead of emitting fabricated unknown metadata.
body:
## Summary

- stack base: #432
- preserve the exact EasyEDA manufacturer part number in generated component metadata
- report a clear conversion error when EasyEDA does not provide a manufacturer part number instead of emitting fabricated `"unknown"` metadata
- update existing inline expectations to match their exact supplier fixtures

## Root cause

`convertBetterEasyToTsx` normalized the manufacturer part number for both the TypeScript identifier and component metadata. This altered real manufacturer metadata such as `XC6206P302MR-G`.

The first fix also used unclear `rawPn` / `pn` names and assigned `"unknown"` as a real manufacturer part number when the source field was absent. That obscured the value's meaning and produced false BOM metadata.

The converter now checks the nullable EasyEDA field at its input boundary. When present, it keeps `manufacturerPartNumber` unchanged end-to-end and derives `componentName` separately. When absent, it reports `Missing manufacturer part number for <LCSC number>`. The generator's existing required-string contract remains unchanged.

## Validation

- C9972 exact-MPN regression passes
- missing-MPN regression passes and reports `Missing manufacturer part number for C9972`
- full network-enabled suite: 137 passed, 0 failed, 56 snapshots
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`

body:
## Summary

- add the real EasyEDA fixture for JLCPCB part C82173 (SY7201ABC)
- add focused characterization coverage showing the current importer emits the six-pin LED driver IC as a discrete `<led>`

## Why

The component's EasyEDA tag is `LED Drivers`. The current category matcher treats any standalone `LED` token as a discrete LED, so generated TSX uses `LedProps`, an `LED1` default designator, and `<led>` instead of preserving the IC as a chip.

This is the reproduction base of a two-PR stack. It intentionally captures the existing behavior without changing production code. The follow-up fix is #431 and is based on this branch, so its diff contains only the classifier change and corrected expectations.

## Validation

title: Keep LED driver ICs as chips
description: Fixes the classification of LED driver ICs to ensure they are treated as chips rather than discrete LEDs, preventing misclassification in the converter.
body:
## Summary

- stack base: #430
- keep `LED Driver` and `LED Drivers` categories out of the discrete-LED classifier
- update the C82173 reproduction to require `ChipProps` and `<chip>` output
- retain existing discrete LED behavior

## Root cause

`categoryValueContainsLed` matched the standalone `LED` token inside the category `LED Drivers`. That category describes an integrated driver circuit, not an LED component.

The fix adds one category guard before the existing LED checks. No component-specific override or pin-count heuristic is introduced.

## Validation

- full network-enabled suite: 136 passed, 0 failed, 56 snapshots

title: Repro : circular BGA pads converting to rectangular pads
description: Reproduces a bug where circular EasyEDA BGA pads are incorrectly converted to rectangular pads in the tscircuit converter.
body:
## Summary

Adds a focused regression reproduction for C2055640 (`STM32L462VEI6TR`, UFBGA-100) showing that circular EasyEDA BGA pads are converted into rectangular tscircuit pads.

## Reproduction

The EasyEDA footprint contains 100 non-drilled `ELLIPSE` pads. Each pad has equal width and height, so these are circular BGA land pads.

The reproduction verifies that:

- the source contains exactly 100 `ELLIPSE` pads;
- every source pad has equal width and height;
- the converter produces exactly 100 PCB SMT pads;
- the expected output shape is `circle`.

The final expectation is marked with `test.failing` because the current converter emits `rect` for every pad.

## Visual evidence

Adds `C2055640-circular-bga-pad-repro.snap.svg`. The snapshot renders all 100 converted BGA pads as squares, making the source/output shape mismatch visible.

## Root cause

The SMT pad conversion currently maps EasyEDA `ELLIPSE` directly to `rect` in `convert-easyeda-json-to-tscircuit-soup-json.ts`.

This PR intentionally contains only the reproduction and snapshot; it does not implement the fix.

## Impact

This changes physical copper geometry for BGA footprints. Square pads have additional copper at their corners compared with the circular lands in the source footprint, which can also affect derived solder-mask or paste geometry.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/C2055640-to-ts.test.ts`
- Result: 2 passing tests, including the expected-failure reproduction.
- Snapshot inspection: 100 rectangular PCB pad elements and 0 circular PCB pad elements.

title: Add appearance controls for the assembled enclosure
description: Adds an independent hiddentranslucentopaque display state for the single assembled enclosure entity Core emits today.
body:
Adds an independent hidden/translucent/opaque display state for the single assembled enclosure entity Core emits today.

## Compatibility representation

This PR does not consume `cad_fdm_enclosure` and does not render separate base/lid records. It structurally recognizes the current compatibility shape:

`source_component → zero-size do-not-place pcb_component → cad_component.model_jscad`

The adapter is isolated in `isLegacyFdmEnclosure`, so the later typed per-part migration can delete it without spreading ID/name heuristics through the renderer.

## Appearance

- translucent by default, so the enclosure does not hide the board it surrounds
- opaque for inspecting the generated print
- hidden for unobstructed board work
- one `Enclosure` item in the Appearance menu, matching the current single CAD entity
- viewer-owned state only; no Circuit JSON display property is added

## Validation

- TypeScript, format, build, focused visibility/detection tests and duplicate-helper gates pass
- the full local suite has the same five pre-existing failures reproduced on upstream main in a clean worktree: two faux-board Z expectations and three headless SVG baselines; this branch changes none of those paths

This belongs to the focused `merge-fdm-enclosure` effort alongside Core #3152. Typed multi-part rendering remains a later Circuit JSON migration.

## Resolved-owner detection

Core initially creates the synthetic PCB owner at zero size, then updates its width/height to the resolved enclosure footprint. The compatibility adapter therefore identifies the final record by its generated JSCAD floor anchor plus do-not-place, off-board and non-obstructing ownership flags; it does not rely on the initial zero dimensions.

## Storybook follow-up

The existing-record Storybook fixture is staged separately for focused review: https://github.com/addibble/3d-viewer/pull/1. It will be opened upstream after this appearance layer merges.

title: Clear overlapping different-net copper pours
description: Batch copper pours by owning subcircuit to apply different-net pour priority and clearance, preserving each pours net, layer, margins, outline, and solder-mask setting, while converting repro172 from an expected failure to a passing PCB snapshot.
body:
## Summary

- update `@tscircuit/copper-pour-solver` from 0.0.44 to 0.0.46
- batch copper pours by owning subcircuit so the solver can apply different-net pour priority and clearance
- preserve each pour's net, layer, margins, outline, and solder-mask setting when inserting per-region solver output
- convert repro172 from an expected failure to a passing, annotated PCB snapshot

## Root cause

Core previously launched one independent solver operation per `<copperpour>`. Each operation could see pads and traces, but not the other pour regions, so different-net pours could occupy the same copper area. Solver 0.0.46 adds coordinated multi-region solving, but core must submit the owning subcircuit's pours in one input problem.

## Validation

- `bun test` across all 18 test files containing `<copperpour>`: 27 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

Depends on tscircuit/copper-pour-solver#77.

title: Render interpolated PCB trace widths
description: Adds support for rendering interpolated PCB trace widths as filled polygons, improving the visual representation of traces in the circuit-to-svg library.
body:
## Summary

- honor `pcb_trace.route_thickness_mode === "interpolated"`
- render connected same-layer segments as a filled polygon whose outline follows each route point's width
- preserve the existing round-capped stroked-segment rendering for `"constant"` and unspecified modes
- render interpolated soldermask traces with the same tapered geometry
- interpolate the width at copper-pour clipping boundaries so a clipped taper remains continuous

## Root cause

circuit-to-svg previously ignored `route_thickness_mode`. Every route pair became an independent SVG stroke using the starting route point's width, so explicitly interpolated traces appeared as abrupt width steps instead of necking continuously into pads.

This adds a separate path only for explicit interpolation. Connected segments are grouped per layer, expanded into one polygon, transformed to SVG coordinates, and emitted as a filled trace path. Existing traces without the flag retain their previous rendering.

## Visual coverage

![Interpolated trace necking into pads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/refs/heads/agent/add-interpolated-trace-support/tests/pcb/__snapshots__/interpolated-trace-necking.snap.svg)

The fixture matches the explicit necking oracle added to [circuit-to-canvas #274](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/pull/274).

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 20000` — 313 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check` — exits successfully with the existing oversized Game Boy fixture diagnostic

title: Add footprinter string backfill and lookup API
description: Add a production D1 footprinter_strings table keyed by numeric LCSC ID, allowing for the storage and retrieval of footprinter strings based on copper IoU thresholds, along with a new API for querying these strings.
body:
## Summary

- add the production D1 `footprinter_strings` table keyed by numeric LCSC ID
- store `footprinter_string` only when `copper_iou > 0.95`, while allowing nullable results for attempted components without a qualifying match
- derive mappings sequentially with `circuit-json-to-footprinter` from EasyEDA Circuit JSON
- add a manually dispatched, production-serialized workflow that runs for at most 60 minutes, batches writes, handles rate limits, and flushes completed work on timeout or termination
- expose `GET /api/footprinter_strings/:lcsc` for numeric or `C`-prefixed identifiers
- return API results under the `component_footprinter_details` top-level key, with nullable matches preserved
- return `404` for unprocessed components and `400` for invalid identifiers without long-lived caching

## Impact

This creates a queryable LCSC-to-tscircuit-footprinter mapping, an incremental production backfill, and a direct lookup API. Existing component/search response contracts are unchanged.

## API

```http
GET /api/footprinter_strings/C2906861
```

```json
{
  "component_footprinter_details": {
    "lcsc": 2906861,
    "footprinter_string": "sod723_p0.865mm_pw0.54mm_pl0.57mm",
    "copper_iou": 0.9923751612092405,
    "updated_at": "2026-08-12 04:34:12"
  }
}
```

## Validation

- `bun test`: 199 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
- local Wrangler Worker smoke test covered `200`, `400`, and `404` responses
- applied all migrations to local Wrangler D1 and verified nullable rows plus the strict greater-than-95% constraint
- applied `0004_footprinter_strings.sql` to production D1 with Wrangler
- ran a three-component production backfill: 3 recorded, 3 matched, 0 failed
- queried the persisted production rows: minimum IoU `0.9923751612`; 0 invalid rows at or below the threshold

title: Improve benchmark comparison comments
description: Replace the separate main and PR benchmark summary tables with one compact Solver  Metric  Main  PR  Change comparison table, add timing rows for P60, P70, P80, and P90, and calculate timing percentiles from solved and timed-out samples while excluding non-timeout failures.
body:
## What changed

- Replace the separate main and PR benchmark summary tables with one compact `Solver / Metric / Main / PR / Change` comparison table.
- Add P60, P70, P80, and P90 timing rows alongside P50 and P95.
- Calculate timing percentiles from solved and timed-out samples, while continuing to exclude non-timeout failures.
- Apply the same percentile behavior to same-machine benchmark comments.
- Keep previous-main and PR per-sample results available in collapsed details.

## Why

The previous comment layout made readers scan between separate tables to compare a metric. Timing percentiles also excluded timeout durations, which could make a slower or less reliable run appear faster.

## Example

| Solver | Metric | Main | PR | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pipeline7 | Completion | 50.0% (🕒50.0%) | 100.0% | +50.0 pp |
| Pipeline7 | Relaxed DRC pass | 50.0% (🕒50.0%) | 100.0% | +50.0 pp |
| Pipeline7 | Timeouts | 1 | 0 | -1 |
| Pipeline7 | P50 time | 1.5s | 1.4s | -10.0% |
| Pipeline7 | P60 time | 1.6s | 1.4s | -10.0% |
| Pipeline7 | P70 time | 1.7s | 1.5s | -10.0% |
| Pipeline7 | P80 time | 1.8s | 1.6s | -10.0% |
| Pipeline7 | P90 time | 1.9s | 1.7s | -10.0% |
| Pipeline7 | P95 time | 1.9s | 1.8s | -10.0% |
| Pipeline7 | Average vias | 2.00 | 2.20 | +10.0% |

_Timing percentiles include solved and timed-out samples. Negative timing changes are faster._

## Validation

- `bun test tests/benchmark-comment-comparison.test.ts tests/benchmark-summary-percentiles.test.ts tests/same-machine-benchmark-results.test.ts tests/pr-benchmark-command.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- Parsed the workflow YAML and compiled both embedded benchmark-comment scripts as async JavaScript functions.

title: Add standalone same-machine benchmark comparison
description: Add an opt-in same_machine_compare mode to the existing autorouter benchmark workflow, allowing for sequential benchmarking of the current main and PR head on the same machine to reduce timing noise and improve comparison accuracy.
body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in `same_machine_compare` mode to the existing autorouter benchmark workflow
- make `/benchmark --same-machine` and `/benchmark-all --same-machine` work as authorized PR comments
- resolve the target PR's current base and head SHAs at dispatch time
- run both revisions sequentially in the same fixed 8-vCPU Blacksmith job
- safely forward regular `benchmark.sh` arguments to both revisions while consuming `--same-machine` as a workflow modifier
- post one PR comment headed `Same Machine Benchmark Results`
- upload both raw JSON/text reports and snapshot HTML files
- keep the benchmark controller checkout separate so the target PR does not need to contain this workflow or renderer

## Why

The existing PR benchmark compares a fresh PR run with a cached main artifact, which can introduce runner-to-runner timing noise. This mode makes relative runtime comparisons meaningful by keeping runner type, machine allocation, dependency setup order, benchmark arguments, and worker limits shared within one workflow job.

This PR contains benchmark infrastructure only; it does not change routing code or dependencies.

## PR comment usage

Authorized owners, members, and collaborators can comment:

description: Protects autorouter benchmark integrity by ensuring that physically invalid benchmark boards do not affect DRC results, leading to improved accuracy in autorouting evaluations.

## Impact

This protects autorouter benchmark integrity: DRC improvements can no longer come from physically invalid benchmark boards.

Using canonical Pipeline 7 at effort 1, the validated dataset changes:

| Metric | Previous dataset | Validated dataset |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Completed | 85/85 | 85/85 |

Five boards become newly DRC-clean: `circuit114`, `circuit134`, `circuit137`, `circuit142`, and `circuit148`. The remaining failures—`circuit018`, `circuit140`, and `circuit143`—are real routing-clearance issues rather than invalid source placements.

## Root cause

The autorouter was pinned to dataset01 before its placement-quality gate. Some benchmark inputs contained impossible physical layouts, including plated holes over SMT pads, cross-net footprint overlaps, and components outside the board. - validates rendered Circuit JSON with tscircuit's official `runAllPlacementChecks`

- repairs 22 affected circuit placements
- keeps the benchmark snapshots in the dataset PR body rather than this repository

No autorouter solver code changes in this PR.

Fixes an issue where `jscad-to-gltf` silently ignored hex string colors (like `#fff`) and defaulted everything to white. This was causing components to disappear completely when rendered in `poppygl` due to GLTF buffer mismatches.

**Changes:**
- `toColorTuple` now correctly hands off string colors to `parseColorValue` (which already knows how to decode hex, rgb(), and named colors).

title: Preserve interpolated necking while fixing variable-width joins
description: Fixes rendering issues with variable-width traces by preserving interpolated necking and correcting the handling of route thickness modes in the canvas implementation.
body:
## Summary

- select trace rendering from Circuit JSON's `route_thickness_mode`
- preserve the filled-polygon path for explicit `"interpolated"` traces so necking remains continuous
- use overlapping round-capped segments for `"constant"` or unspecified traces, fixing the sharp U1/VM geometry
- apply the same mode-aware behavior to soldermask rendering
- add the focused necking fixture from #275 alongside the U1/VM reproduction from #272

## Root cause

The U1/VM trace contains changing route-point widths but does not set `route_thickness_mode`. The previous canvas implementation treated any changing width as interpolated and built a single offset polygon, creating acute spikes at abrupt width changes.

The first version of this PR overcorrected by removing interpolation entirely. The correct discriminator is the Circuit JSON field:

- `route_thickness_mode === "interpolated"`: continuously blend route-point widths with the existing polygon renderer
- `"constant"` or missing mode: draw each segment at its own width with round caps

This keeps legitimate pad necking while fixing the original U1/VM rendering bug.

## circuit-to-svg finding

circuit-to-svg currently ignores `route_thickness_mode` and renders per-segment paths using the starting route point's width. The necking comparison intentionally exposes that difference; SVG is not used as the semantic oracle for explicit interpolation.

## Visual coverage

### Explicit interpolated necking

![Canvas and SVG necking comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/refs/heads/agent/fix-variable-width-trace-joins/tests/elements/__snapshots__/pcb-trace-necking.snap.png)

### U1/VM non-interpolated trace

![U1 VM comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/refs/heads/agent/fix-variable-width-trace-joins/tests/board-snapshot/__snapshots__/ti-boost-drv8848-u1-vm-pad.snap.png)

## Validation

- `bun test` — 153 passed
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check` — clean aside from the existing oversized Game Boy fixture warning

title: Reproduce interpolated trace necking
description: Add a focused visual fixture for a wide top-layer trace necking down before two SMT pads, opting into continuous width blending with route_thickness_mode: interpolated.
body:
## Summary

- add a focused visual fixture for a wide top-layer trace necking down before two SMT pads
- opt into continuous width blending with `route_thickness_mode: "interpolated"`
- compare circuit-to-canvas and circuit-to-svg at a tight, pad-focused viewport
- leave renderer behavior unchanged so this PR establishes the visual contract first

## What the investigation found

- [circuit-json](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/blob/main/src/pcb/pcb_trace.ts) defines `route_thickness_mode` as `"constant" | "interpolated"`, with `"constant"` as the default. Consumers should therefore only blend vertex widths when the field is explicitly `"interpolated"`.
- [pcb-viewer](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-viewer/blob/main/src/lib/convert-element-to-primitive.ts) follows that contract: explicit interpolated traces become an expanded polygon; all other traces become individual line primitives.
- circuit-to-svg does not currently inspect `route_thickness_mode`. It creates [per-segment paths](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/blob/main/lib/pcb/svg-object-fns/create-svg-objects-from-pcb-trace.ts) using the [starting route point's width](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/blob/main/lib/pcb/get-pcb-trace-segments.ts), so the lower half of this snapshot shows abrupt steps rather than a taper.
- The TI BOOST-DRV8848 U1/VM trace from #272 has changing route-point widths but no `route_thickness_mode`. That means it belongs on the non-interpolated path, while this new fixture protects legitimate necking from the change proposed in #274.

## Visual oracle

![Canvas and SVG necking comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/refs/heads/agent/reproduce-interpolated-trace-necking/tests/elements/__snapshots__/pcb-trace-necking.snap.png)

title: Use smooth inverse-distance lens calibration
description: Replaces Delaunaybarycentric calibration with Shepard inverse-distance weighting, preserving global translation, rotation, and scale with an affine baseline, and blending measured residual corrections using inverse-square weights.
body:
## What changed

- replace Delaunay/barycentric calibration with Shepard inverse-distance weighting
- preserve global translation, rotation, and scale with an affine baseline, then blend measured residual corrections from every CSV point using inverse-square weights
- use an analytic Jacobian for Newton inversion
- regenerate the calibration model and STM32 distorted snapshot
- add dense full-board checks for invertibility, continuity, and folding

## Why

Selecting three points through a Delaunay triangle makes the derivative change abruptly at triangle boundaries, and adding many calibration points can create visually apparent seams. The IDW residual field is continuous across the complete board and does not change behavior when a nearest-neighbor set changes.

Inverse-square weighting remains exact at every calibration point and continuously differentiable there. On the current 15-point CSV, leave-one-out RMS improves from about 1.798 for the Delaunay model to 1.747 for IDW.

## Validation

- `bun run check`
- 12 tests pass
- STM32 and RP2040 snapshots match
- TypeScript, builds, and LightBurn export pass

title: Tessellate LightBurn paths before lens distortion
description: Flatten straight and cubic Bzier LightBurn primitives into line segments no longer than 0.5 mm, applying piecewise-linear calibration to every generated sub-vertex, preserving path topology, and adding tessellation tests.
body:
## Summary

- flatten straight and cubic Bézier LightBurn primitives into line segments no longer than 0.5 mm
- apply the piecewise-linear calibration to every generated sub-vertex instead of only original endpoints/control handles
- preserve closed/open path topology and expose the default segment-length constant
- add focused line and Bézier tessellation tests and update the STM32 distorted-output snapshot

## Root cause

The calibration is nonlinear across the Delaunay mesh. Transforming only a primitive’s endpoints leaves the interior as one unchanged straight/Bézier primitive, so it cannot follow changes in the transform between calibration triangles.

Tessellation happens in board coordinates before distortion. Each sub-vertex is then transformed independently, allowing long paths to bend where the calibration changes.

## Validation

- `bun run check` (11 tests, STM32/RP2040 snapshots, builds, LightBurn export)
- targeted Biome check for every changed source/test file
- line test verifies each 0.5 mm intermediate vertex against `designToProjected`
- Bézier test verifies curves are flattened and endpoints remain exact
- updated STM32 LightBurn snapshot visually inspected

title: Use piecewise-linear lens calibration
description: Replaces the smoothing TPS with a Delaunay-triangulated piecewise-affine calibration derived from the latest 15-point CSV, ensuring zero residual at all calibration points and improving interpolation accuracy.
body:
## Summary

- replace the smoothing TPS with a Delaunay-triangulated piecewise-affine calibration derived from the latest 15-point CSV
- use barycentric interpolation inside each triangle so every measured calibration coordinate maps exactly
- use continuous convex-hull/affine extrapolation outside the measured region
- tessellate straight and Bézier LightBurn paths to segments no longer than 0.5 mm before transforming every generated point
- preserve the deprecated bilinear matrix export, update inverse mapping, and refresh the STM32 distorted-output snapshot

## Why

The regularized TPS intentionally smooths through the measurements, leaving a 0.6684 training RMS, so individual measured points can still appear off. Piecewise-linear interpolation has **zero residual at all 15 calibration points**.

Choosing the three nearest samples independently is unsafe here because multiple samples on the right edge share `X = 32.5`; the nearest triple can be collinear and singular. A deterministic Delaunay mesh provides standard nondegenerate neighboring triples and keeps interpolation continuous across shared edges.

Nearest-triangle extrapolation outside the convex hull can become non-injective near hull vertices. This implementation instead maps the nearest hull edge and extends outward with the global affine Jacobian. A 75 × 45 mm grid round-trips with maximum error below `1e-10`.

A nonlinear transform applied only to existing endpoints leaves each intervening LightBurn primitive unchanged. The export now flattens lines and cubic Béziers in board coordinates first, then transforms each sub-vertex, so distortion is represented along the complete path.

## Validation

- `bun run check` (11 tests, STM32/RP2040 snapshots, builds, LightBurn export)
- targeted Biome check for all changed source/test files
- calibration generator reproduced the checked-in 21-triangle model
- line and Bézier subdivision tests verify independently transformed intermediate points
- updated STM32 LightBurn snapshot visually inspected

title: Use a thin-plate spline for lens calibration
description: Replaces bilinear lens calibration with a regularized thin-plate spline (TPS) for improved accuracy in lens distortion correction, while maintaining compatibility with the previous bilinear model.
body:
## Summary

- replace the bilinear lens calibration used by LightBurn export with a regularized thin-plate spline (TPS), a standard smooth 2D registration transform
- regenerate the TPS coefficients from the corrected coordinate CSV and include all 15 calibration points
- preserve the old 2×4 matrix export as a deprecated bilinear baseline for API compatibility
- invert the TPS with its analytic Jacobian and update the STM32 distorted-output snapshot

## Why

The corrected CSV no longer contains the bad via 10 measurement. On all 15 points, the regularized TPS (`λ = 1`) lowers training RMS from **1.1369** for the bilinear baseline to **0.6684** (about a **41% reduction**) while retaining smooth behavior instead of exactly interpolating every sample. The generated fit metadata also records the 1.8262 leave-one-out RMS for visibility.

## Validation

- `bun run check`
- targeted Biome check for every changed source/test file
- calibration generator reproduced the checked-in model
- STM32 lens-distortion snapshot visually inspected

title: Derive forward lens distortion from coordinate CSV
description: Derives the constrained 2  4 bilinear calibration matrix from the committed via-coordinate-map.csv and applies the forward design-to-projected transform to lens distortion files, ensuring accurate LightBurn geometry representation.
body:
## Summary

- derive the constrained 2 × 4 bilinear calibration matrix from the committed `via-coordinate-map.csv`
- add a reproducible `bun run generate:lens-calibration` workflow and a sync regression test
- apply the forward design-to-projected transform to `*-lensdistortion.lbrn2`, including the fitted positive translation
- preserve LightBurn-compatible CutSettings while cloning shapes, avoiding lowercase boolean serialization
- update the STM32 lens-distortion snapshot and public API names to reflect forward distortion

## CSV fit

The deterministic fit uses the basis `[1, X, Y, XY]` independently for projected X and Y with iterative 3-sigma rejection.

Via 10 is the only rejected measurement: its projected Y value (`30.621`) is inconsistent with nearby measurements at the same design Y and otherwise degrades the all-point RMS to `13.68`. The retained 14-point fit has:

- RMS error: `1.1714`
- maximum retained residual: `2.4290`
- excluded vias: `[10]`

Generated matrix:

```
[
  [83.65980006195808, 1.0221134297130683, 0.016303536111300976, -0.0002240949113389866],
  [71.69211041573234, -0.022282848652282874, 1.0235176817866805, -0.0010984548152200868],
]
```

## Why

The previous export mixed inverse correction with board-local translation, which moved the LightBurn geometry in the wrong direction. The lens-distortion artifact represents predicted measured/projected coordinates, so it must center the board design coordinates and apply the forward fitted model.

title: Serialize CutSetting booleans as numeric values
description: Serializes all boolean CutSetting properties as numeric values (0 or 1) to ensure compatibility with LightBurn, preventing project opening errors.
body:
## Summary

- serialize every boolean CutSetting property as LightBurn-compatible `0` or `1`
- update the existing power-ramp snapshot to use the canonical representation
- add regression coverage for true and false values across `enablePowerRamp`, `perforate`, `dotMode`, `crossHatch`, and `wobbleEnable`

## Why

The CutSetting property serializer only handled `crossHatch` and `wobbleEnable` specially. Other boolean fields fell through to `String(value)`, producing lowercase `true` and `false`. LightBurn rejects those values while opening an LBRN2 project with errors such as:

```
Could not convert XML Attrib 'perforate' = 'false' to Bool
```

LightBurn-authored files use numeric boolean values for CutSetting properties, so applying the existing `0`/`1` convention consistently prevents invalid projects.

## Impact

Projects created or reserialized with boolean CutSetting values can now be opened by LightBurn without manual XML edits.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 56 passing
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`

body:
## Problem

The routing analysis currently chooses the closest three components using the smallest distance on any single axis. That produces misleading neighbors.

For example, the Arduino snapshot reported `C7` next to a congestion region spanning x=6.7–13.9 mm even though `C7` ends at x=-17.2 mm. The component was roughly 24 mm away horizontally, but it was selected because it was close on the Y axis. The same report exposed the resulting geometry as:

```text
distToLeftEdgeOfRegion="-25.5mm"
```

This makes the diagnostic noisy and prevents the CLI from reliably using the result for severity scoring or actionable placement suggestions.

## Change

- calculate physical edge-to-edge distance between component and region bounding boxes:
  - `dx = max(horizontal gaps, 0)`
  - `dy = max(vertical gaps, 0)`
  - `edgeDistanceMm = hypot(dx, dy)`
- include intersecting components plus components whose physical body is within 5 mm
- store bounds, edge distance, overlap depth, and directional free space as numbers
- include `overlapDepthMm` only when the component overlaps the region
- format measurements only in `getString()`
- remove the arbitrary closest-three selection

A `NearbyComponent` does not carry a `relation="nearby"` field. Membership in `nearbyComponents` already communicates that. Overlap is represented only by the optional numeric `overlapDepthMm`.

## Result

- large components are included when their body is close even if their center is far away
- components that are close on one axis but far away on the other are excluded
- displayed edge distances are never negative
- overlap remains available separately for future congestion scoring
- the Arduino example no longer reports physically distant components such as `C7` for that region

## Tests

Regression coverage verifies:

- a component 0.7 mm from the region is included
- a large component with a distant center but nearby body is included
- a diagonally distant component is excluded
- a component 25 mm away is excluded
- overlap has zero edge distance and positive overlap depth
- serialized distances are not negative

## Validation

- `bun test`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`

## What changed

title: Compact candidate-hop state for faster routing
description: Reduces memory allocation for candidate hops by indexing them by legal portregion pairs, improving routing performance and memory efficiency.
body:
## Summary

- index candidate hops by legal port/incident-region slots instead of every impossible port/region pair
- use compact generation-scoped typed arrays for queued/closed frontier state and best costs
- prune closed/dominated candidates before intersection and region-cost scoring, and reduce heap index writes
- reuse finite 2D distance calculations in core and outside-in routing hot paths
- turn the DDR5 4.21 GB allocation repro into a passing solver-construction test (662 KB candidate state)

## Same-machine benchmarks

Fresh sequential SRJ18 runs at concurrency 1 against `main` (`8fc61cf`):

| Metric | Main | PR | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Total completion | 22.182 s | 14.080 s | 1.575x |
| Average solveGraph | 2.477 s | 1.520 s | 1.630x |
| P50 | 1.571 s | 1.065 s | 1.475x |
| P95 | 7.715 s | 5.052 s | 1.527x |
| Route completion | 100.0% | 100.0% | unchanged |
| Average final region cost | 1.739 | 1.739 | exact match |

All eight SRJ18 final costs matched main exactly. Two earlier full pairs also measured 1.597x and 1.642x average solveGraph speedups.

The PR's paired Blacksmith workflow was stronger: total time improved from 96.256 s to 35.407 s (2.72x), average solveGraph from 11.362 s to 3.811 s (2.98x), and P95 from 54.274 s to 13.435 s (4.04x). Completion remained 100%. Average final region cost moved from 1.713 to 1.739 (+1.5%); main's sample008 hit the 2,000,004-iteration cap, while the PR completed it in 1,197,441 iterations. [Same Machine Benchmark Results](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/pull/164#issuecomment-5263044765)

Full HG07 (105 samples) improved from 5.751 s to 4.600 s total (1.250x), with all per-sample statuses, completion values, and final costs identical to main.

Sample008 process-tree peak RSS fell from 1,656,032 KiB to 836,272 KiB (-49.5%). Its dense best-cost arrays shrink from 1,215.2 MiB to 0.50 MiB.

Accepted and rejected trial details are in `experiments/compact-candidate-hop-state.md`.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --pretty false`
- `bun test --timeout 9999999 --max-concurrency 1` — 119 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`
- full SRJ18 and HG07 main-vs-PR comparisons at concurrency 1

title: Pair every PR benchmark with main on one runner
description: This PR changes the benchmarking process to run every authorized tiny-hypergraph benchmark command on the current main and the PR head sequentially on the same runner, ensuring consistent comparison results.
body:
## Summary

- make every authorized tiny-hypergraph `/benchmark` PR comment compare current main with the PR head
- lock both revisions when the comment is received
- check out, install, and benchmark both revisions sequentially in one Blacksmith job
- forward the exact same safely parsed `benchmark.sh` arguments to both revisions
- remove the cached main-artifact comparison path
- report both SHAs and the runner name in a `Tiny Hypergraph Same Machine Benchmark Results` comment
- retain raw reports and per-revision result artifacts
- allow paired comment runs up to 120 minutes because they execute both revisions

## Why

The previous command benchmarked the PR in a fresh run, then compared it with the newest successful main artifact from a different workflow run and potentially a different machine. Runner variance could therefore look like a routing improvement or regression.

After this PR, a `/benchmark` result is paired by construction: main runs first and the PR runs second in the same job, on the same allocated runner, with identical arguments.

## PR comment behavior

Examples remain unchanged:

- `/benchmark`
- `/benchmark --limit 4`
- `/benchmark --dataset srj18 --concurrency auto`
- `/benchmark --dataset hg07 --limit 20 --solver poly`

Every one of these now produces a same-machine main-versus-PR comparison. The instructions posted on new PRs describe the paired behavior.

## Validation

- workflow and instruction YAML parsed successfully
- focused parser/workflow test: 1 passed, 0 failed (16 expectations)
- full test suite: 116 passed, 0 failed
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check` (passes with the pre-existing oversized-fixture warning)
- `git diff --check`

## Deployment note

GitHub evaluates `issue_comment` workflows from the default branch. The new slash-command behavior therefore becomes active for all PRs as soon as this PR is merged.

title: Speed up tiny-hypergraph routing hot paths
description: Reduces repeated distance, angle, incidence, and reservation work in the core and outside-in routing loops, leading to improved performance without affecting routing output stability.
body:
## Summary

- reduce repeated distance, angle, incidence, and reservation work in the core and outside-in routing loops
- reject closed hops before candidate scoring and reduce indexed-heap map writes with hole-based sifting
- index committed route segments once per partial-rip round
- remove temporary allocations from selective rerip blocker searches
- document retained and rejected optimization trials, including memory measurements

## Performance and quality

On isolated SRJ18 `sample008` runs, median solveGraph time improved from about 6.65s on untouched `main` to 4.73s (about 1.4x faster).

Routing output remained stable:

- 361/361 routes completed on sample008
- sample008 max region cost remained 3.391
- all eight committed SRJ18 cases retained 100% completion
- every reported final region cost matched its committed baseline

Two initially faster experiments were deliberately excluded: clearing sparse maps on every route and storing a parallel heap hop-key array. Both increased measured RSS. The retained single-board peak remained within repeated untouched-main variance.

The complete experiment log is in `experiments/tiny-hypergraph-phase-speed.md`.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- 20 focused core, indexed-heap, distance-aware, outside-in, selective-rerip, reservation, and region-cost tests
- `git diff --check`
- `./benchmark.sh --concurrency 1`: 8/8 success, 100% route completion, unchanged reported region costs

A local full test run reported 108 passing tests. Three visualization-backed files could not start because this checkout was missing the native `sharp-darwin-arm64v8.node` binary; this was a local dependency installation issue rather than a test assertion failure.

body:
## Summary

- pin the benchmark adapter to the merged, validated generation-v2 SRJ29 BGA decoupling dataset and fail fast if an invalid/older manifest is loaded
- map depth-indexed signal buses to their intended board face
- add `preferOriginalEndpointTracks`, which projects each boundary route onto the real downstream pad coordinate and strongly prefers the pad/source layer when legal
- preserve plane-aware VCC/GND breakout, DRC-gated endpoint completion, and the invariant that layer-transition vias lie along trace interiors rather than at endpoints
- count a sample as solved only when every original endpoint is physically connected and the complete emitted copper passes independent DRC
- regenerate composite and per-layer SVG snapshots for passing samples 001, 005, and 009

## Root cause

The previous signal strategy optimized compact breakout tracks at the fanout boundary, not the coordinates and layers of the actual outside pads. A fanout could therefore look orderly near the BGA but stop beside its destination, leaving endpoint completion to recover with long global routes. The corrected dataset made this mismatch especially visible.

The new strategy aligns boundary tracks with the real destination pads during fanout and favors same-layer assignments. Same-layer traces enter the pads directly; the few necessary layer changes occur at legal interior points along existing traces.

## Impact

The updated snapshots are deliberately gated by fanout validation, original-endpoint connectivity, and routed-copper DRC:

- `sample001`: 23/23 connected
- `sample005`: 50/50 connected
- `sample009`: 25/25 connected

Full 200-sample Blacksmith run, 6 layers, 256 assignment budget, concurrency 32, and a 180-second per-sample ceiling:

| Metric | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Strictly solved samples | 159/200 |
| Fanout prefixes | 7,880/8,050 (97.9%) |
| Original endpoints physically connected | 7,769/8,050 (96.5%) |
| Independently DRC-clean complete attempts | 198/200 |
| Partial / errors / timeouts | 39 / 0 / 2 |
| Wall time | 212.03s |

The 39 partially connected samples and two timeouts are not marked solved. This keeps the benchmark honest about endpoint connectivity instead of rewarding visually adjacent or boundary-only breakouts.

## Validation

- `bun test`: 68 pass, 0 fail, 98,282 assertions
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`
- full 200-sample benchmark on a Blacksmith 32-vCPU runner
- 21 SVG snapshots: composite plus six individual copper layers for three strictly solved samples

title: [BENCHMARK TEST] Independently validate SRJ29 endpoints and emitted copper
description: Adds an independent physical-copper connectivity validator for original SRJ endpoints, ensuring emitted copper connects to original endpoints and meets DRC requirements before marking a sample as solved.
body:
## What changed

- add an independent physical-copper connectivity validator for original SRJ endpoints
- model matching-layer contact through wires, vias, and same-net pads
- reject boundary-only traces and cross-layer visual overlaps that do not electrically reach the destination pad
- independently audit every emitted wire and via against different-net pads, obstacles, traces, and vias across its physical layer span
- reject unsupported virtual layer transitions and disconnected trace/via sequences
- require fanout validation, original endpoint connectivity, and emitted-copper DRC before the SRJ29 benchmark marks a sample solved
- report fanout-prefix progress separately from physically connected original connections

## Root cause

The benchmark treated any continuous BGA-to-boundary prefix as a completed connection. `buildOutputSimpleRouteJson` retained the original downstream endpoint as metadata, but neither the solver validator nor benchmark proved that emitted copper reached it. Clearance validation also inspected accepted route-plan objects instead of independently auditing all emitted copper, leaving future auxiliary traces outside the benchmark gate. This allowed arbitrary boundary exits on the wrong coordinate and layer to count as solved and made the benchmark vulnerable to unaudited completion traces.

## Local impact

The three visual samples that previously passed are now honestly classified:

- sample001: partial, 21/21 fanout prefixes, 0/21 original connections physically connected
- sample005: partial, 48/48 fanout prefixes, 0/48 connected
- sample009: partial, 19/19 fanout prefixes, 2/19 connected

The first corrected Blacksmith run found the real baseline: **0/200 solved**, **7,459/7,676 fanout prefixes (97.2%)**, but only **19/7,676 original connections physically connected (0.3%)**. The latest commit adds the independent emitted-copper DRC gate and triggers a replacement Blacksmith run.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 61 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- targeted acceptance/rejection tests for same-layer pad contact, cross-layer overlap, vias, boundary-only traces, different-net pad/trace intersections, via span collisions, and virtual layer transitions
- local sample001/sample005/sample009 runs: all remain partial for endpoint connectivity; all three existing fanout outputs pass the independent emitted-copper DRC

title: Consolidate unobstructed parallel same-net traces
description: Consolidates parallel same-net trace segments by pulling one segment onto anothers centerline, ensuring the corridor is free of obstacles and foreign-net traces, while retaining clearance validation and geometry.
body:
## Summary

- detect same-layer, same-net trace segments with parallel overlapping projections
- pull one segment onto the other segment's centerline for the common run, preserving each trace's declared endpoints
- require the entire swept corridor to be free of obstacles and foreign-net traces before consolidating
- retain the existing clearance validation and 45-degree chamfer pass for the approach/departure geometry
- update the RP2040 beautification snapshot and documentation

## Why

The existing same-net consolidation only reused copper between coordinates that two routes already shared. Offset traces could run beside one another for a long distance with empty space between them and never combine. This change makes those spans render and manufacture as one shared copper path for the duration of their parallel overlap.

## Safety

Candidates are rejected when:

- the traces are on different layers or are not parallel
- the common run is too short to leave shared copper after the 45-degree approaches
- an obstacle intersects the swept corridor
- a foreign-net trace crosses or occupies the corridor
- the replacement fails the existing obstacle/foreign-net clearance check

## Real-board impact

The fixed RP2040 reproduction increases from 0 to 14 same-net consolidations while retaining zero clearance violations and all fixed-via invariants.

## Validation

- `bun run test` — 26 tests passed
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- focused RP2040 SVG snapshot passed on macOS and x86_64 Linux with Bun 1.3.14
- visually inspected the updated RP2040 snapshot; pads and prefabricated vias remain present

## Dependency

This is a focused follow-up to merged PR #9.

title: Add mandatory pre-expansion trace beautification
description: Summary add an always-on BeautifyBiscuitBoardTracesSolver between clearance cleanup and power-trace expansion opportunistically increase board-wide clearance toward 0.4 mm while falling back to the already-valid route on constrained boards consolidate same-net spans between shared junctions when reuse does not lengthen the connection replace unprotected Manhattan corners with the largest clearance-safe 45 chamfer show only the active final route in completed pipeline visualizations so superseded corner geometry is not rendered as live copper preserve board outlines, pads, obstacles, terminals, and prefabricated vias in beautification visualizations expose beautification stats, document the pipeline, and maintain fixed-via, RP2040, and STM32 visual snapshots  Why The router previously guaranteed minimum clearance and could simplify broad stair-step runs, but it did not optimize the cleaned result for visual spacing or deliberately reuse same-net copper before the power-trace expander widened routes.  Impact Beautification now always runs before power-trace expansion. Every candidate preserves terminals and fixed-via boundaries, is checked against obstacles and foreign nets, and the complete output is revalidated before expansion. Chamfers reserve the 0.4 mm aesthetic-clearance target locally to leave room for nominal-width expansion. The fixed-via regression asserts that the removed 90 corner coordinates are absent from the final route. The RP2040 and STM32 real-board tests assert that beautification materially changes their post-processed routes, creates 45 chamfers, and renders labeled pad and prefabricated-via geometry in their SVG snapshots.  Validation bun run format:check bun run build bun test (23 passing tests, including STM32 and RP2040 real-board repros)
body:
## Summary

- add an always-on `BeautifyBiscuitBoardTracesSolver` between clearance cleanup and power-trace expansion
- opportunistically increase board-wide clearance toward 0.4 mm while falling back to the already-valid route on constrained boards
- consolidate same-net spans between shared junctions when reuse does not lengthen the connection
- replace unprotected Manhattan corners with the largest clearance-safe 45° chamfer
- show only the active final route in completed pipeline visualizations so superseded corner geometry is not rendered as live copper
- preserve board outlines, pads, obstacles, terminals, and prefabricated vias in beautification visualizations
- expose beautification stats, document the pipeline, and maintain fixed-via, RP2040, and STM32 visual snapshots

## Why

The router previously guaranteed minimum clearance and could simplify broad stair-step runs, but it did not optimize the cleaned result for visual spacing or deliberately reuse same-net copper before the power-trace expander widened routes.

## Impact

Beautification now always runs before power-trace expansion. Every candidate preserves terminals and fixed-via boundaries, is checked against obstacles and foreign nets, and the complete output is revalidated before expansion. Chamfers reserve the 0.4 mm aesthetic-clearance target locally to leave room for nominal-width expansion.

The fixed-via regression asserts that the removed 90° corner coordinates are absent from the final route. The RP2040 and STM32 real-board tests assert that beautification materially changes their post-processed routes, creates 45° chamfers, and renders labeled pad and prefabricated-via geometry in their SVG snapshots.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- `bun test` (23 passing tests, including STM32 and RP2040 real-board repros)

Passing --layer top or --layer bottom reaches the same CLI error.  Known DRC findings The routed result has two real same-layer, different-net clearance violations, but the independent shorts check finds no direct shorts: a top-layer GND trace is 0.068 mm from U_CORE_BUCK.EN (0.1 mm required) a FLASH-supply via is 0.083 mm from a PSRAM-supply trace (0.1 mm required) Also, setting only minViaHoleDiameter0.3mm currently produces 0.3 mm outer-diameter vias. body:
## Summary

- update `tscircuit` to `0.0.2289`
- remove the direct capacity-autorouter dependency and all custom routing phases
- remove breakout/fanout routing, manual PCB paths, explicit escape vias, and route post-processing
- route the entire design with the board's built-in autorouter
- set the board's minimum via drill diameter to 0.3 mm

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck`
- `npx tsci check source`
- `npx tsci check placement`
- `npx tsci check schematic-placement`
- `npx tsci build --site --autorouter-timeout 5m`
- `npx tsci check shorts --mode pcb dist/index/circuit.json` — no shorts detected

The literal Gerber-mode `npx tsci check shorts dist/index/circuit.json` currently exits before checking because the four-layer renderer reports `Inner layer inner1 only supports copper gerbers`. Passing `--layer top` or `--layer bottom` reaches the same CLI error.

## Known DRC findings

The routed result has two real same-layer, different-net clearance violations, but the independent shorts check finds no direct shorts:

- a top-layer GND trace is 0.068 mm from `U_CORE_BUCK.EN` (0.1 mm required)
- a FLASH-supply via is 0.083 mm from a PSRAM-supply trace (0.1 mm required)

Also, setting only `minViaHoleDiameter="0.3mm"` currently produces 0.3 mm outer-diameter vias. Adding a conventional 0.6 mm pad diameter causes `PowerTraceExpanderSolver` to run out of iterations and emit no route, so that broader manufacturability change is intentionally not included here.

body:
## Summary

- Add the complete `BOOSTXL-TMP107` tscircuit project from the current local engineering source, based on commit `fa81393e9c677864fcebe27fc8827d88113c23c8`.
- Preserve the circuit, component values, pin connections, footprints, supplier metadata, UART selection, and two breakaway TMP107 sensor nodes.
- Improve schematic fidelity with a connected powered-triangle projection for U1, tighter trace-label spacing, and TI-proportioned TMP107 coupon frames and placement.
- Refine the UART conditioning area by repositioning R1 and R2 and rotating R1 vertically to match the local reference layout.
- Add the PCB, schematic, and 3D snapshots generated by `tsci`.
- Register the board in the repository catalog and shared TypeScript configuration.

## Repository scope

This follows the source-only layout of the existing TI BoosterPack projects: TSX sources, board documentation, and canonical snapshots only. It intentionally excludes Gerbers, exports, PDFs, caches, dependency directories, standalone configs, and local STEP/OBJ files. Component wrappers reference their 3D assets on the tscircuit model CDN.

The circuit body is byte-identical to the local source after its four import declarations. The import-only changes flatten the paths for this repository and replace local model-file imports with CDN URLs.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build` — all 4 circuits passed
- `bunx tsci check shorts boostxl-tmp107/index.circuit.tsx --mode gerber --layer all` — no shorts detected
- `bunx tsci snapshot boostxl-tmp107/index.circuit.tsx --3d --disable-parts-engine` — PCB, schematic, and 3D snapshots all match

## Model note

The production identity remains the exact `TMP107BIDR` / JLCPCB `C2870479`. Because that SKU's EasyEDA model endpoint was unavailable, the CDN 3D asset comes from the pin-compatible SOIC-8 record `C2870960`; the electrical and supplier metadata are unchanged.

## Summary

- classify ordinary two-pin fixed SMD resistors from their `R?` prefix, standard resistor package, and resistance-valued metadata
- normalize EasyEDA resistance values to tscircuit inputs, including zero-ohm links such as `0Ω` → `0ohm`
- generate `<resistor>` with `ResistorProps` instead of the generic `<chip>` path
- preserve each imported JLCPCB code, exact manufacturer part number, inline footprint geometry, package-specific pad dimensions, and OBJ/STEP model URLs
- omit imported custom schematic symbols for resistor primitives
- add table-driven regression coverage for C17168, C11702, C25744, C2929994, and C107701

## Root cause

The TypeScript converter had specialized generation paths for several standard primitives but no resistor path. Standard SMD resistors therefore fell through to the generic chip generator, which emitted `ChipProps`, `<chip>`, and potentially an imported custom schematic symbol.

## Reproduction

Before this change:

```sh
bunx tsci import C17168 --jlcpcb --use-exact-footprint
```

generated `A_0402WGF0000TCE.tsx` with `ChipProps` and `<chip>`. With this change, the converter emits `ResistorProps`, `<resistor resistance="0ohm">`, the same exact two-pad R0402 footprint, and the original C17168 OBJ/STEP models.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/convert-to-ts/smd-resistors-to-ts.test.ts` — 5 cases, 100 assertions

## Changes

- emit semantic `<diode>` components only for two-pin diode parts
- fall back to `<chip>` for multi-pin diode arrays
- preserve C96225's six-pin electrical and footprint interface
- use the chip box symbol for the fallback so all six pins and labels are evenly aligned and readable

- update the C96225 3D snapshot

title: Fix cross-sheet net label collision handling
description: Fixes cross-sheet net label collision handling by treating direct endpoints crossing schematic-sheet boundaries as solver-visible connections and refining the rules for net label generation to prevent overlaps.
body:
## Summary

- treat direct endpoints that genuinely cross a schematic-sheet or subcircuit boundary as solver-visible cross-boundary connections
- feed same-subcircuit cross-sheet fallback labels into normal solver placement and collision handling
- preserve existing collapsed-box behavior for internal connections omitted from a boxed subcircuit solver pass
- validate all eight BOOST-DRV8711 cross-sheet gate-drive labels plus the stacked schematic snapshot

## Root cause

Core detected only direct traces that crossed a subcircuit boundary. A direct trace crossing only a schematic-sheet boundary left one visible endpoint in each per-sheet pass, but was not added as a single-port solver net connection. Its fallback label was therefore inserted after routing and collision handling, allowing it to overlap neighboring labels.

The initial scope check was too broad: it treated any endpoint omitted from the current solver pass as externally connected. Collapsed schematic boxes intentionally omit their internal components, so this exposed generated internal names such as `U1_STATUS` and `load_GND`. The refined rule requires an actual subcircuit boundary or an endpoint represented outside the current schematic sheet and not on it.

## Impact

Cross-sheet direct connections now use the same general label-solver pipeline as existing cross-subcircuit connections, while internal collapsed-box connections remain hidden. Sheet membership is checked directly from `schematic_port.schematic_sheet_id` against the current render pass; there are no global sheet-set intersections, board-specific placement exceptions, coordinate offsets, or dependency changes.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repros/repro173-boost-drv8711-cross-sheet-netlabel-overlap.test.tsx tests/repros/repro-boxed-subcircuit-internal-port-name-leak.test.tsx tests/repros/repro154-subcircuit-exposed-port-schematic-connections.test.tsx`
- `bun test tests/repros/repro-subcircuit-cross-boundary-fallback-label.test.tsx tests/repros/repro-subcircuit-cross-boundary-trace-name-label.test.tsx tests/repros/repro140-multi-sheet-shared-bus-net-label-collapses-to-one-sheet.test.tsx tests/features/schematic-sheet/schematic-sheet04.test.tsx tests/features/schematic-sheet/schematic-sheet05.test.tsx`

title: Remove Sharp from SVG snapshot comparison
description: Removes the transitive dependency on Sharp for SVG snapshot comparison by using Resvg for rasterization and image-utils for comparison, ensuring visual comparison and PNG diff generation without Sharps installation issues.
body:
Rasterizes SVG snapshots with `@resvg/resvg-js`, then compares the PNG output through `@tscircuit/image-utils/looks-same`.

This removes the transitive chain:

```text
bun-match-svg → looks-same@9 → sharp@0.32.6 → install-time libvips download
```

while preserving visual comparison, metadata-insensitive matching, and PNG diff generation.

Motivation: all Core test shards failed before running tests when Sharp's GitHub libvips download returned `socket hang up`; its native fallback then failed because system libvips was absent. A clean install of this branch contains no Sharp package.

Validation: package typecheck, 7 tests, format, and all PR gates pass.


## Prior art

This is the same comparison pipeline introduced in [tscircuit/core#3059](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3059) (`b026f224`, “Use image-utils for snapshot tests”): rasterize SVG with Resvg, then compare/diff PNGs through `@tscircuit/image-utils/looks-same`.

Core #3059 removed Core's direct Sharp/`looks-same@9` usage, but `bun-match-svg` still retained the transitive `looks-same@9 → sharp@0.32.6` path. This PR completes that earlier migration at the package that owns SVG snapshot matching.

title: Open the new build logs after GitHub sync
description: Changes the GitHub sync process to wait for new build logs to be available before navigating to the build detail page, ensuring users see the latest logs instead of stale ones.
body:
## Summary

- snapshot the package's existing non-PR build IDs before starting a manual GitHub sync
- poll the package releases API until it exposes a different latest build ID
- navigate to that exact release/build detail page, which displays the new build logs
- share the behavior between desktop and mobile package sidebars
- add unit coverage for both a new release and a same-release rebuild
- add a desktop/mobile Playwright regression test that proves navigation waits for the new build

## Why

The GitHub sync endpoint only queues asynchronous worker jobs. Navigating as soon as it returns can open the previous release and its stale logs.

The updated flow waits until the API exposes the new build. This works whether the worker creates a new package release or rebuilds an existing release with a new build ID. If no new build appears within two minutes, the user stays on the package page and sees a message that the sync is still queued.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test ./src/lib/wait-for-new-package-build.test.ts` (2 passed)
- `bunx playwright test playwright-tests/github-sync-navigation.spec.ts --retries=0` (2 passed)

title: Increase footprinter request rate
description: Raises the EasyEDA request-start ceiling from 2 to 4 requests per second and increases concurrent component workers from three to four while retaining existing cooldown and error handling mechanisms.
body:
## Summary

- raise the shared EasyEDA request-start ceiling from 2 to 4 requests per second
- increase concurrent component workers from three to four
- retain the existing global two-minute cooldown and automatic reduction to 1 request per second after any EasyEDA 403
- update the README with the production settings

## Why

The first optimized production run issued 6,523 EasyEDA requests over 3,557 seconds (1.83 requests/second), indexed 3,448 records, and encountered zero 403 responses or cooldowns. This increases the ceiling while keeping request starts globally paced and preserving immediate adaptive backoff.

## Safety behavior

Requests remain evenly spaced rather than bursty. The first EasyEDA 403 globally pauses queued requests for two minutes, leaves affected components retryable, and limits the rest of the run to 1 request per second.

## Expected impact

The practical throughput will depend on EasyEDA latency and the four-worker pipeline, but the new ceiling allows up to roughly 2 components per second for the usual two-request component lookup. Final workflow metrics report actual request rate, cooldown count, CPU utilization, conversion time, and D1 timing.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 209 passing
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx biome format .`
- `git diff --check`

title: Speed up footprinter string population
description: Optimizes the population worker to process three components concurrently while implementing a shared limiter for EasyEDA requests, enhancing throughput and efficiency in data handling.
body:
## Summary

- process three components concurrently while routing every EasyEDA request through one shared limiter capped at two request starts per second
- pause all queued requests for two minutes after an EasyEDA 403, then reduce the remainder of the run to one request per second
- increase production D1 read batches from 25 to 250 and write batches from 10 to 50
- report EasyEDA, conversion, D1, and CPU timing metrics at the end of each run
- retain graceful deadline and signal handling, incremental writes, stock-first ordering, and retry eligibility for transient failures

## Why

The population worker previously made two EasyEDA requests per component sequentially and spawned a Wrangler process for every 25 reads and 10 writes. A full run averaged about 1.5 EasyEDA requests per second and indexed 2,674 records. Small component concurrency can hide request latency, while the shared limiter keeps traffic bounded and non-bursty. Larger D1 batches remove substantial local process overhead without increasing EasyEDA traffic.

## Expected impact

The explicit EasyEDA ceiling is only about 33% above the observed average request rate from the latest successful run. Expected throughput is roughly 3,200–3,600 components per hour, with automatic backoff if EasyEDA signals a limit.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 209 passing
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx biome format .`
- `git diff --check`

title: Record permanent footprinter source misses
description: Classifies definitive EasyEDA source misses separately from transient failures and records them as nullable footprinter_strings rows, improving the backfill process by making it idempotent for components that EasyEDA definitively does not contain.
body:
## What changed

- classify definitive EasyEDA source misses separately from transient failures
- record definitive misses as nullable `footprinter_strings` rows
- retain retries for rate limits, timeouts, HTTP 5xx responses, parsing failures, and Wrangler failures
- report permanent misses and retryable failures separately in workflow logs

## Why

The backfill previously left every thrown lookup error unrecorded. As a result, components that EasyEDA definitively does not contain were selected and attempted again on every default workflow run.

The default query already skips existing nullable rows, so recording permanent misses makes the backfill idempotent for those components. The manual `retry_null_entries` workflow input remains available when an intentional refresh is needed.

## Validation

- `bun test` (206 passed)
- `bun run format:check`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

title: Add SVG snapshot for acute line joins
description: Add a focused toMatchSvgSnapshot regression case for a thick, acute polyline and capture the current mitered SVG rendering as the baseline.
body:
## Summary

- add a focused `toMatchSvgSnapshot` regression case for a thick, acute polyline
- capture the current mitered SVG rendering as the baseline

## Why

The existing line snapshots use straight two-point segments, so they cannot reveal a line-join regression. This fixture creates an intentionally sharp corner with a thick stroke, making the current pointed miter easy to see and giving the round-line-join fix in the stacked PR a meaningful SVG snapshot diff.

This PR contains only the reproduction and baseline snapshot. PR #229 will be retargeted on top of this branch with the renderer change and updated rounded snapshot.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `git diff --check`

title: Render lines with round joins
description: Emit stroke-linejoinround for lines in generated SVGs and use round line joins in canvas and PNG rendering paths to ensure consistent line appearance across renderers.
body:
## Summary

- emit `stroke-linejoin="round"` for lines in generated SVGs
- use round line joins in canvas and PNG rendering paths
- assert that every generated line polyline carries the round join
- update the acute-polyline SVG snapshot from a pointed miter to a rounded bend

## Stack

- Base/repro: #230 adds a focused `toMatchSvgSnapshot` fixture and captures the current pointed miter
- This PR applies the renderer fix and contains the resulting SVG snapshot diff

## Why

Exported SVG lines fell back to SVG's miter join default, even though the interactive renderer already used rounded joins. Canvas rendering likewise only configured rounded end caps. This makes line appearance consistent across renderers and avoids sharp spikes at polyline corners.

The stacked snapshot uses a thick, acute V-shaped polyline. Before accepting the new snapshot, the matcher produced a visual diff highlighting the old triangular miter beyond the new rounded bend.

## Validation

- `bun test` (69 passing)
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`

The autorouter visualization emitted every routed segment as a separate two-point polyline. `stroke-linejoin="round"` only rounds vertices inside one polyline, so neighboring segments still met as independently capped shapes and produced the notch visible at acute corners. Emitting each continuous routed run as one polyline gives the SVG renderer a real vertex to round.

title: Add CI check for string ID hacks
description: Adds a CI workflow to check for hard-coded string ID prefixes in newly added production lines, preventing potential coupling of solver behavior to naming conventions.
body:
## What changed

- add a `No String ID Hacks` workflow for pull requests and pushes to `main`
- inspect only newly added production lines under `lib/`
- reject hard-coded underscore-delimited prefixes passed to `startsWith(...)`, including multiline calls
- emit an inline GitHub Actions annotation directing contributors to explicit metadata or discriminated unions
- add focused coverage for expression detection, comment handling, multiline calls, and unified-diff parsing

## Why

Inferring circuit entity types from encoded ID strings (for example, checking `source_trace_`, `pcb_trace_`, or `source_net_`) couples solver behavior to naming conventions and can silently break when IDs change. A deterministic diff check catches this precise anti-pattern without requiring an API key or nondeterministic AI review.

Existing code is not grandfathered into every run: the scanner checks only newly added `lib` lines, so this introduces no repository-wide cleanup requirement.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- focused unit test: 1 pass, 0 failures
- checker against `main..HEAD`: passes
- checker against historical commit `4fdce4f4`, which introduced `startsWith("missing_connection_")`: fails with the expected file/line annotation
